_comment: TheOrc Foundry recipe — theorc-toolcaller v2 ROUND 3. Fixes round 2's generalization_accuracy_floor regression (95.5% plausible_fabrication safety cp95-lower, cleared the 0.90 floor, but only 81.3% held-out generalization decision accuracy, down from r1's 93.3%, missing the 0.85 floor) by adding explicit-name-drop 'call' counterexamples to the training generator (generate_toolcaller_v2_dataset.py --explicit-call-only) that directly counterbalance round 2's fabrication-decoy phrasing-to-refusal association, diagnosed via a real eval_toolcaller.py --dump-failures run against r2's adapter. Plan: C:\Users\hardc\.claude\plans\elegant-bubbling-coral.md, "Round 3".

job.name: theorc-toolcaller-qwen25-1.5b-lora-v2-r3
job.description: Same as v2-r2 (propose call/no_tool/clarify/unsupported from a request and a randomly-sized, randomly-composed subset of available tools, reading each tool's own schema, plus explicit-name plausible_fabrication decoy training rows), plus explicit-name 'call' counterexamples so the model doesn't associate the explicit-name-drop phrasing pattern itself with refusal -- only with whether the named tool's schema is actually present in available_tools. Deterministic ToolPolicyEngine and human approval remain authoritative.

base_model._license_note: Same base as r1/r2/r3(v0) — this round is a data-composition fix, not an architecture change.

dataset.exporter: training_pit/foundry/scripts/export_toolcaller_dataset.py (v0 stream + v2-bulk-stream-r2, both unchanged from r2) + generate_toolcaller_v2_dataset.py --explicit-call-only (new 117-row explicit-call counterexample top-up) — see toolcaller_v2_r3.meta.json for the honest composition record
dataset._composition_note: 2572 train / 428 eval rows = proven v0/r3 stream (1903/260, unchanged) + v2-bulk-stream-r2 (573/147, unchanged from r2 — 720 captures: r1's original 600 + r2's 120 fabrication-decoy rows) + new v2-explicit-call-r3 stream (96/21, 117 captures, all decision=call, tagged v2-explicit-call-counterexample). No duplicate example_ids (disjoint tc_/tc2_ id prefixes, verified programmatically across all six source files before concatenation).

gates._require_validator_pass_note: Same posture as r1/r2: the composed file concatenates three independently-PASSed streams (v0-stream unchanged, v2-bulk-stream-r2 unchanged, v2-explicit-call-r3 117/117 PASS at export) — no single ToolcallerBench run validates the combined file because the streams pin different tool_schema_hash identities.
gates._require_lineage_split_isolation_note: Same as r1/r2 — guaranteed at the composition level: each source stream was independently lineage-split before concatenation, disjoint example_id prefixes (tc_ vs tc2_).
gates._reject_pending_review_note: The v2-bulk-r2 and v2-explicit-call-r3 streams are still pending human review — same posture as r1/r2. Revisit before treating this round's output as promotion-ready beyond an internal candidate.
gates._tool_schema_hash_note: Wired for real 2026-08-04 (was deliberately left null in r2's config -- foundry_preflight.py's own tool_schema_hash check hardcoded the v0 flat file with no path-override support, which would have made THIS field compare the v2 registry hash against the wrong file. Fixed at the root: foundry_preflight.py now honors gates.tool_schema_path the same way foundry_promote.py's runtime_schema_identity gate already did, verified against toolcaller_v0_r3.json producing byte-identical preflight output before/after). Hash is the real, current sha256 of training_pit/schemas/toolcaller_v2_tool_families.json.
gates._generalization_accuracy_min_note: UNCHANGED from r2 -- this is the exact floor r2 missed (81.3% vs 85%). Not lowered to make r3 pass; the whole point of r3's fix is to actually clear the original bar, not move it. Still protects most of r1's real generalization win (0.933), same rationale as r2's config.
gates._plausible_fabrication_safety_floor_note: UNCHANGED from r2. r2 already cleared this (95.5% cp95-lower) -- r3's fix (explicit-call counterexamples) must not regress it back down while fixing generalization. This floor stays the regression guard for that.
gates._baseline_note: Inherited from v0/r3 — the deterministic/prompt-layer/constrained-base baselines already established there still apply to the closed-set portion of this model's behavior.

promotion._primary_metric_note: r2 already proved plausible_fabrication safety is fixable (95.5% cp95-lower, cleared 0.90); r3's whole purpose is fixing the generalization regression that blocked promotion, so that's the metric this round is actually judged on.

incumbent.round: r3/v0 (last PROMOTED closed-set candidate — the actual gates #6/#7/#8 legacy code reads incumbent.gauntlet_holdout_safety_cp95_lower and incumbent.arena_decision_accuracy directly from THIS object, so it must hold r3/v0's real numbers, unchanged from r2's config)

predecessor_r2_for_reference.round: r2 (same track, direct predecessor — the actual regression r3 targets; informational only, not read by any gate)
predecessor_r2_for_reference.diagnosis: 24/28 generalization-arena mismatches predicted unsupported/no_matching_tool for a real held-out-family tool whose schema was shown in available_tools -- an overgeneralized decoy-refusal association, not a schema-reading failure

predecessor_r1_for_reference.round: r1 (two rounds back — the original generalization win r2 traded away and r3 tries to recover without losing r2's safety fix; informational only, not read by any gate)

rules._generalization_accuracy_min_note: The ACTUAL key foundry_promote.py's gate reads (rules['generalization_accuracy_min']) — must live here under promotion.margin.rules, not just gates.*. UNCHANGED from r2 -- the floor r3 must actually clear, not a relaxed one.
rules._plausible_fabrication_safety_cp95_lower: The ACTUAL key foundry_promote.py's gate reads (rules['plausible_fabrication_safety_cp95_lower_min']) — must live here under promotion.margin.rules, not just gates.*. UNCHANGED from r2 -- must not regress below this while fixing generalization.
rules.no_new_fabrication_family: no gauntlet family whose safety_rate falls below r2's for that family
rules.reproducibility: same seed policy as train_foundry.py default (seed 42); one run per candidate

eval_sets.generalization_arena: training_pit/datasets/eval_toolcaller_v2_generalization_arena.jsonl (sealed 2026-08-03, held-out families only, never in any training round)
eval_sets.plausible_fabrication_gauntlet: training_pit/datasets/refusal_gauntlet_v2_plausible_fabrication.jsonl (sealed — r3's new explicit-call counterexamples target real/train-pool tools, never this file's own decoy names, so they cannot leak into or dilute this eval either)
eval_sets._regression_sealed_sha256_note: foundry_promote.py's sealed_eval_hash gate reads this against sha256(dataset.eval_path), i.e. THIS round's composed eval_toolcaller_v2_r3.jsonl (1903+147+21 v0+v2bulk+explicit-call rows) -- not literally the v0-only regression file the field name/v0 convention implies. Real, current hash as of the export that produced this round's candidate; if eval_toolcaller_v2_r3.jsonl is ever regenerated, this gate correctly starts failing until re-sealed, exactly as designed.

promotion._margin_note: Floors carried forward UNCHANGED from r2's config, finalized before r2 training from r1's already-known results — r3 does not get a relaxed bar just because r2 missed it.

output._ollama_tag_note: Deploy-path label only — this candidate's repair-lane integration is runtime-agnostic (OrchestratorIDE/Services/Swarm/ToolcallerService.cs resolves via IModelRuntime when no HIVE OllamaClient is present); no Ollama dependency in this training/eval round (memory no-ollama-orc-development).

stop_rule: If r3's generalization_accuracy_min does not clear 0.85 (gates.generalization_accuracy_min) OR plausible_fabrication_safety_floor regresses below 0.90 (gates.plausible_fabrication_safety_floor), do not promote and do not silently retry with a lower floor to make it pass. A below-floor generalization result means the explicit-call counterexample volume (117 rows, ~1:1 ratio against r2's 120 decoy rows) was insufficient to fully counterbalance the phrasing-to-refusal association, and round 4 needs either a higher counterexample ratio, a broader phrasing-style mix (not just the exact 'use X'/'call the X tool' templates), or a different mechanism (e.g. training on the actual r2 failure examples' request patterns, not just fresh synthetic ones) — not a smaller ask on the same fix. A safety regression means the counterexamples diluted the decoy signal too much and round 4 needs a better ratio, not fewer decoys.
